claims.visible_claim: This page places Extraversion—social engagement, active expression, and positive emotion—within the Big Five continuous-domain framework ([S1](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2283588/)). The six facets below use NEO/IPIP-NEO vocabulary. The official IPIP resource says its scales measure constructs similar to NEO facets, while the BFI-2 uses a different 15-facet architecture ([S11](https://ipip.ori.org/Finding_Scales_to_Measure_Particular_Constructs.htm); [S2](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27055049/)). These labels must not be treated as fully equivalent across instruments.
claims.boundary: Supports the continuous domain and facet vocabulary, not social skill, diagnosis, scale equivalence, or product validity.

claims.visible_claim: A meta-analysis of longitudinal research reported group-average change in some personality traits across the life course, but it cannot predict how one person, one specific facet, or a fixed age point will change ([S4](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16435954/)).
claims.boundary: Group-average longitudinal findings do not provide an individual trajectory or fixed timetable.

claims.visible_claim: FermatMind has not published product-level reliability, validity, Chinese norms, or individual predictive evidence for the scores discussed by this package. This material is for self-observation and education. It is not for clinical diagnosis, hiring screening, school admission, or replacing a career decision.
claims.boundary: Public product and method boundary; not an empirical research claim.
